Chapter 9. Sustaining Your Own Energy and Growth as a Manager.
Lifting others up? That takes real energy. And if you want to keep doing it well, you’ll need to make sure you’re caring for yourself, too.
Think about those flight attendants who always remind you to put on your own oxygen mask before helping others. It’s the same idea here—leaders need to recharge and grow if they’re going to be there for their teams.
So, what does this look like in real life? Let’s talk about some habits that help managers stay energized and keep growing.
First up, regular reflection. Take a little time each week to look back on what’s going well, what’s been tough, and what you’re picking up along the way. Whether you jot down your thoughts in a journal or talk things through with a peer, making space for reflection brings clarity and fresh insight.
Next, seek feedback. Really open yourself up to honest input from your team, your peers, or even a mentor. When you ask for feedback, you’re not just finding your blind spots—you’re also showing humility and a willingness to learn. That’s powerful.
Then, set boundaries. Guard your downtime and make space for family, hobbies, and rest. When you model a healthy work-life balance, you give your team permission to do the same—and that benefits everyone.
And don’t forget about continuous learning. Invest in yourself. Read a new book, attend a workshop, or connect with other managers and swap stories. Every bit of growth you experience helps you bring more to your team.
Here’s a quick story—a manager at a fast-paced startup was burning out fast. She started blocking off just one hour a week for her own reflection and learning. That simple shift helped her regain her energy and perspective. And you know what? Her team noticed the difference, too. Everyone thrived.
So, here’s the key takeaway. The same practices that lift others up? They apply to you as well. When you nurture your own growth and well-being, you show up as a more resilient, empathetic, and effective leader. And your team will feel the impact.
